# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024): 1B.9 evidence note

Overall read: **mildly favorable, low confidence**. I found 2024 evidence that Pakistan under Sharif kept dual-use / catastrophic-risk issues inside formal institutional and multilateral channels, including cyber, AI, outer space, and nuclear-safety discussions. I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of reckless handling, but the record is mostly institutional rather than a clear ruler-level precaution/transparency initiative.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Pakistan-China Bilateral Consultations on Arms Control and Nonproliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-09-14 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistan-china-bilateral-consultations-on-arms-control-and-nonproliferation | Pakistan said the talks covered global/regional security, **cyber, AI, outer space**, peaceful nuclear technology, and multilateral treaty forums. That is direct evidence of handling dual-use / catastrophic-risk issues through formal diplomacy rather than informal or opaque channels. | 1B.9; also 1B.4, 1B.7 |
| Favorable | The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-10-21 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan | Pakistan briefed UN disarmament fellows on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and its nuclear safety/security architecture. This supports a precautionary, institution-facing posture and some transparency toward external experts. | 1B.9; also 1B.4, 1B.3, 1B.7 |
| Favorable | Pakistan’s nuclear-security regime page | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Updated in May 2024; standing page | https://mofa.gov.pk/vienna-pakistans-nuclear-safety-seccurity-regime | The official page says Pakistan updated its nuclear-security regime booklet in May 2024, renewed practical arrangements with the IAEA, and places the NCA/SPD in a formal oversight structure. That is indirect but strong evidence of institutionalized precaution. | 1B.9; also 1B.3, 1B.7 |
| Favorable | Arms Control And Disarmament | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Standing policy page; current version cites a May 2024 update | https://mofa.gov.pk/arms-control-and-disarmament | Pakistan’s policy page says it supports IAEA safeguards, export controls, UNSCR 1540 implementation, reciprocal inspections proposals, CTBT objectives, and a unilateral testing moratorium. It also says Pakistan joined the Nuclear Security Contact Group. This is the clearest public-facing precaution/transparency posture on sensitive technologies. | 1B.9; also 1B.4, 1B.3, 1B.6 |
| Favorable | Message on the Occasion of Youm-e-Takbeer on 28th May 2024 | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-05-27 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/25454 | The government described Pakistan as a responsible nuclear state committed to stringent controls and comprehensive safety measures. This is institutional, not personal, but it supports a precautionary stance toward catastrophic-risk domains. | 1B.9; also 1B.3, 1B.5, 1B.6 |

## Search gap

- I did **not** find strong 2024 evidence of Sharif personally announcing new cyber, AI, or biological-risk legislation, transparency measures, or crisis-reporting protocols.
- I also did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that he handled these domains recklessly or through secrecy.
- So the best-supported conclusion is that his 2024 record is **precautionary by institutional posture**, but there is **limited direct ruler-level evidence** on biological or cyber governance specifically.
